data.exact_reserve_text: Favourable movements of GBP 15.1 million, (2015: GBP 16.0 million), in the past year's provision for claims outstanding, net of expected reinsurance recoveries, are included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance. These arose in respect of the following classes of business:
data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2016 the syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding was GBP 327.927m. During 2016 the syndicate recorded a gross prior-year release of GBP 12.896m (about 3.93% of opening gross reserves) shown in the technical provisions reconciliation as "Change in prior year provisions" (gross -GBP 12.896k). The net impact (after reinsurer's share) is described as a favourable movement of GBP 15.123m. The movement is principally described as favourable claims development with associated reinsurance recoveries. The technical provisions note also shows a material RITC intake on reserves (gross GBP 148.677m) which affects comparatives and totals.
raw_causal_phrases: Favourable movements of GBP 15.1 million, (2015: GBP 16.0 million), in the past year's provision for claims outstanding, net of expected reinsurance recoveries, are included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Primary gross prior-year movement sourced from the Technical Provisions reconciliation table row 'Change in prior year provisions' (gross (12,896) thousand). The report also states a net favourable movement of GBP 15.123k (net of reinsurance) in narrative - both figures are present and consistent (gross release of 12.896k + reinsurers' share release of 2.227k = net 15.123k). Lob-level movements shown in the 'Claims' note are provided net of reinsurance in the printed table; these were mapped to Lloyd's standard LOB names and included with reduced confidence. A large RITC intake (gross GBP 148.677k) is present in the technical provisions table and can distort simple comparisons of opening/closing reserves; users should be aware the RITC affects balances. Small negative/parenthesised cells in the premiums table (e.g. '(1)') were transcribed as negative small amounts; these are immaterial but flagged.
